panels.rationale: Single non-contrast axial head CT of a human trauma patient showing a large right-sided biconvex (lentiform) hyperdense extra-axial collection consistent with acute epidural hematoma, with 6-mm midline shift; caption and article explicitly attribute this to acute EDH, and measurement annotations (62.84 mm x 40.43 mm) are visible. [raw subtype: acute]

panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography (CT) scan of an 18-year-old bicycle versus vehicle head-on patient Computed tomography (CT) study conducted on an 18-year-old male patient upon the immediate deterioration of the initial presenting condition (GCS 13 to GCS 5 in four hours). This image highlights the presence of a large, acute, right-sided EDH, measuring 62.84 mm by 40.43 mm, as well as a 6-mm midline shift. The patient underwent an immediate craniotomy where the entirety of the EDH was removed. Intraoperatively, a nondisplaced frontotemporal skull fracture was noted. The patient responded positively to the surgical treatment and was discharged on postoperative day four with a complete resolution of the initial and developed conditions. EDH: epidural hematoma
in_text_mentions: A Hispanic male, 18 years of age, presented to the emergency department (ED) after a head-on collision with a vehicle traveling at 30 miles per hours (mph) while riding his bicycle. Our patient initially presented in a promising condition with a Glasgow Coma Score (GCS) of 13, however, this rapidly deteriorated to a GCS of 5 within a four-hour window. Immediate CT studies (Figure 1) revealed the presence of a large, right-sided, acute EDH with a 6-mm midline shift, indicating the need for immediate surgical intervention.

panels.rationale: Sagittal MRI of the cervical spine in a human patient showing a 4.5 × 0.8 cm extradural collection at C5–7 with cord compression and edema, which at surgery proved to be an epidural hematoma; the article title and in-text mentions attribute this finding to spontaneous cervical epidural hematoma. Spinal (cervical) epidural hematoma is a recognized but less common form of epidural hematoma, hence variant. The provided vocabulary is cranial-CT oriented, so the extradural collection is tagged with the closest matching key and the spinal-specific features are proposed.

A: Axial head CT shows a right frontal/temporal biconvex epidural hematoma, a classic imaging manifestation of epidural hematoma; caption and in-text explicitly attribute it to a large epidural hematoma.
